passages.t: Buying a field in a doomed land
passages.happening:
The word comes to Jeremiah in Zedekiah's tenth year, Nebuchadnezzar's eighteenth (verse 1). Babylon's army is besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah is confined in the courtyard of the guard in the palace (verse 2). Zedekiah locked him up for prophesying that the city would fall and the king be taken to Babylon (verses 3 to 5).

God tells Jeremiah that his cousin Hanamel will come and ask him to buy his field in Anathoth, because Jeremiah has the right of redemption (verse 7). Hanamel comes, just as God said (verse 8). ‘So I bought the field in Anathoth from my cousin Hanamel, and I weighed out seventeen shekels of silver’ (verse 9). Jeremiah signs and seals the deed, calls witnesses and weighs the silver (verse 10). He gives both copies of the deed, the sealed one and the open one, to Baruch son of Neriah in front of Hanamel, the witnesses and the Judeans sitting in the courtyard (verses 11 and 12).

He tells Baruch to put the deeds in a clay jar so they will last a long time (verse 14). ‘Houses, fields, and vineyards will again be bought in this land’ (verse 15).
passages.hearers:
The date is about 588 or 587 BC. The siege had begun the year before and would end with the city's fall a year later. Anathoth, Jeremiah's hometown, was already in enemy hands.

The law gave the nearest relative the right, and the duty, to buy back family land when a kinsman had to sell, so that it stayed in the family. Hanamel came to Jeremiah as next of kin. To buy land in a country about to be conquered looked like madness.

Deeds were written in two copies. One was rolled and sealed; the other left open for reading. Storing them in a clay jar protected them for years, the same way the Dead Sea Scrolls were later kept.

This chapter introduces Baruch son of Neriah by name, Jeremiah's scribe and companion, who will write his words down in chapter 36.
passages.later: The law of redemption stood behind the purchase: ‘his nearest of kin may come and redeem what his brother has sold’ (Leviticus 25:25). Boaz redeemed a field for Naomi's family in the same way (Ruth 4:9).
passages.asks: Jeremiah bought land in a country about to fall, because God said it would be bought again. Ask what act of hope you could make now that only makes sense if God keeps his word. And ask whether your faith shows in what you are willing to spend.

passages.t: Is anything too difficult for the LORD?
passages.happening:
After giving the deed to Baruch, Jeremiah prays (verse 16). “Oh, Lord GOD! You have made the heavens and the earth by Your great power and outstretched arm. Nothing is too difficult for You!” (verse 17). He recalls God's love to thousands, his signs in Egypt, the gift of the land, and the people's disobedience (verses 18 to 23). Now the siege ramps are against the city (verse 24). Yet God has told him to buy the field with silver and call witnesses, even though the city is being handed to the Chaldeans (verse 25).

God answers. ‘Behold, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh. Is anything too difficult for Me?’ (verse 27). He will give the city to the Chaldeans, who will burn it (verses 28 and 29), for Israel and Judah have done evil from their youth, turning their backs and not their faces (verses 30 to 33). They put abominations in his house (verse 34) and built high places in the Valley of Hinnom to make their children pass through the fire, something God never commanded nor did it enter his mind (verse 35).

Yet he will gather them from all the lands and bring them back to live in safety (verse 37). They will be his people, and he their God (verse 38). He will give them one heart and one way (verse 39) and make an everlasting covenant never to stop doing them good (verse 40). ‘Yes, I will rejoice in doing them good, and I will faithfully plant them in this land with all My heart and with all My soul’ (verse 41). Fields will be bought again, with deeds signed and sealed and witnessed, all over Judah (verses 43 and 44).
passages.hearers:
Jeremiah's prayer is honest. He praises God's power and then, in effect, asks why he has been told to buy a field in a land about to be lost. He obeyed first and asked afterward.

God's answer turns Jeremiah's own words back to him. Jeremiah said nothing is too difficult for God; God asks whether anything is. The judgment and the restoration are both true, and God will do both.

The Old Testament repeatedly charges Judah with making children pass through the fire, and it names kings who did so. Scholars debate details, such as whether Molech was a god's name or a kind of sacrifice. But Jeremiah's words point to real sacrifice, and the phrase that it never entered God's mind is a strong way of saying it had nothing to do with him.

Heart and soul are the words Israel was called to use in loving God. Here God uses it of his own love for them.
passages.later: God asked Abraham the same question when Sarah laughed: ‘Is anything too difficult for the LORD?’ (Genesis 18:14). The angel told Mary, ‘For no word from God will ever fail’ (Luke 1:37).
passages.hard:
Verse 35 speaks of child sacrifice in the Valley of Hinnom. Did Judah really do this, and what does God mean that it never entered his mind?

The Old Testament repeatedly charges Judah and its neighbors with making children pass through the fire, and it names kings who did so: Ahaz and Manasseh (2 Kings 16:3; 21:6). Scholars debate some details, such as whether Molech was a god or a term for a kind of sacrifice, and whether every reference means a killing or sometimes a dedication rite. But Jeremiah's words about burning sons and daughters (7:31; 19:5) point to real sacrifice, and child sacrifice is attested in the wider ancient world.

The phrase that it never entered God's mind does not mean God did not know of it. It is a way of saying total rejection: this was so far from anything God desired or commanded that it could never be connected with him.

Abuse of a child is a crime. It is to be reported to the police and the proper authorities, not handled quietly inside a church. If a child is in danger, or you know of a child being harmed, contact the police or your local child protection service now. If you were harmed as a child, what was done to you was wrong, and it was not your fault. The Find Help page on this site lists places to turn.
passages.asks: God says he will rejoice in doing his people good with all his heart and soul. Ask whether you picture God as reluctant or as glad to do you good. And ask what seems too difficult in your life that you could bring to him.
